story_type: avalanche filmed on Mount Rainier, slab breaks and powder cloud rolls into trees, 1973 park service film
hook: A whole slope of snow broke loose and raced downhill.
narration: A whole slope of snow broke loose and raced downhill.
This was Mount Rainier in Washington, filmed by the National Park Service in 1973.
A slab avalanche starts when a thick layer of snow cracks free from a weak layer buried underneath.
Once it lets go, the slab shatters into blocks as it slides.
Then the loose snow lifts into the air, and a cloud pours off the ridge.
It kept growing as it dropped, heading for the trees at the bottom.
outcome: The cloud poured into the trees and filled the valley below.
title: Avalanche pours down Mount Rainier
description:
An avalanche on Mount Rainier in Washington State, filmed in 1973: a slab of snow breaks loose, shatters, and sends a powder cloud rolling into the trees below.
